analysis.title: Global Economics Daily Points, November 17, 2026
key_insights: Global equities are defensive ahead of Nvidia earnings after the close, with consensus EPS of US$2.47. Tech is volatile, European and Asian benchmarks and Canadian futures are lower, and US futures are volatile.

Sovereign yields are lower by a handful of basis points in US Treasuries, Canadian government bonds, gilts and euro area government bonds, which Scotiabank reads as some flow into bonds. The dollar is mixed and oil is up a few cents.

Scotiabank doubts the Iran war is over as President Trump claimed. It cites a third US aircraft carrier arriving in the region, intelligence reports of a possible Iranian dirty bomb plot against Washington, and ongoing attacks.

US October retail sales (8:30am ET) are expected to show little to no growth. Scotiabank expects 0.0% headline and 0.2% ex-autos against consensus of 0.1% and 0.4%, and prior readings of 0.8% and 0.9%.

The retail sales control group is the key line. It excludes autos, food, building materials and gas, is more closely tied to total consumer spending, and followed a soft prior month. A weak headline could be offset by a solid control group.

The control group rose about 4.5% q/q SAAR in Q3, so the October print sets momentum into Q4 and the holiday season. Scotiabank notes Black Friday discounting has spread across the year and carries less signal than before.
US October industrial production (9:15am ET) is expected at +0.1% m/m with capacity utilization at 76.9% (Scotiabank) vs 76.8% consensus. Manufacturing output is expected to keep growing moderately.
UK labour data was generally soft. Payroll jobs fell about 34k in October, the biggest drop since November 2020, though the series is often heavily revised. Short-dated gilts rallied modestly.

UK total employment rose 48k in the three months data lag (September), about 150k over two months. The unemployment rate fell a tick to 4.6% in September, the lowest since April 2025. Vacancies keep falling but remain near the long-run average.
UK wage growth slowed to 1.7% m/m SAAR in September, the slowest since late winter. The three-month moving average is 2.9%.

Canadian existing home sales were flat in October (+0.3% m/m SA) after falling over the prior two months following four months of gains. Housing starts are due at 8:15am ET, with Scotiabank at 260k vs 240k consensus and 248.9k prior.

Governor Macklem will not seek another term at the Bank of Canada next June. Scotiabank dismisses media candidate surveys as unreliable and lists qualities the Board and government may want: a strong inflation-target record, sound judgement at inflection points, French bilingualism, forecasting experience and market and private-sector experience.
Scotiabank expects francophone candidates to have the edge for BoC Governor given bilingualism and Quebec sensitivities.

tension_points.theme: US retail sales headline vs control group
tension_points.bull_case: A weak headline could be dominated by a potentially solid control group, which tracks total consumer spending more closely and followed a Q3 gain of about 4.5% q/q SAAR.
tension_points.bear_case: The control group is coming off a fairly soft prior month, so momentum into Q4 may be fading.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak control group print in the 8:30am ET October retail sales release.

theme_stances.key_argument: The control group will set the tone for Q4 consumer momentum even if the headline retail sales number is weak.
theme_stances.evidence: the control group will be key
